messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide launches autonomous ride-share service in Millfield. Price: $0.18 per mile. Average wait time: 15 minutes. Cove
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto sector revenue index: 79 (baseline: 100). Foot traffic and sales are somewhat down.

Patricia Hawkins laid off workers: begin privately processing the emotional weight of the layoffs i made this month. these were people — some of them longtime employees, possibly people my father knew when he ran the original lot. i need to sit with what i did, not just manage the narrative around it. write a private note to myself about each person laid off: what their role was, what they contributed, and what i could realistically do to help them — whether that is a strong reference, outplacement support through angela's transition program, or a direct call to howard liu or other employers in the network who might have need.

Rick Tanner laid off workers: formally commit to producing a location-specific consolidation readiness assessment for millfield auto mall within two weeks — structured around the three-tier framework patricia outlined (ev/av-exposed, transition-ready, anchored roles) but layered with my floor-level knowledge of which techs are certifiable, which salespeople have transferable skills, and what the service lane capacity looks like under a reduced-sales model. not a layoff list. an asset map. i tell patricia this directly in the meeting.

Business closing: Rick Tanner — after the patricia meeting, send a short note to jake morrison acknowledging the under-$22k floor strategy and clearing any internal friction — pull the units, make sure the lot positioning happens, confirm that the month-end close target is supported from the top. i do not micromanage jake's pitch, but i make sure he knows the gm is aligned and not going to undercut him with a competing priority.

Business closing: Jake Morrison — personally work my single best remaining pre-qualified lead — the buyer who came in twice in the past 60 days, looked at a 2021 civic priced at $19,400, said they needed to 'think about it.' i call them directly, not a text, not an email. i run the monthly payment math with them on the phone: $19,400 financed over 60 months at current rates is under $380/month. i offer to hold the unit for 48 hours at that price with no obligation. this is the one i close. i don't pitch the lot — i pitch this specific car to this specific person. if they say no i ask one question: what would it take?

Business closing: Jake Morrison — request a one-on-one with rick tanner this week. not to complain, not to ask for protection — to present value. i bring my last 90 days of personal close data, my pipeline of pre-qualified leads by price tier, and a one-page read on which inventory segments still have buyer interest. i also ask him directly, casually, whether the stay bonus patricia mentioned at the all-hands applies to floor sales staff. i want to know if the $12k is on the table before angela's map goes in and before rick has categorized me without my input.

Business closing: Tamika Jefferson — close the first paying freelance client from the discovery call pipeline. target: the hvac contractor or one of the two restaurants from the tick 2 outreach — whoever showed the most engagement. convert the relationship from 'warm conversation' to a signed agreement: $350/month retainer, three months minimum, two social posts per week plus one monthly short-form video. send a simple one-page agreement via email today. no more 'let's talk soon.' a decision is required.

Subtly reference that the methodology framework is being designed to be repeatable and scalable — planting the seed that this is a proprietary approach, not just an internal spreadsheet.

Do not publish or market yet. This is a private commitment to a defined offering, grounded in the actual work I am doing right now.
